top news.title: Investigation: Polymarket is paying creators to make deceptive videos about winning bets, targeting users in the US, where its primary crypto platform is banned

tweets.author: @neilmhta
tweets.text: - Polymarket made dummy websites mirroring its real site, then paid creators to use the fake site and pretend to win thousands.  - Creators altered headlines and used outdated footage to imply they won bets—even when they often lost - Polymarket paid Adin Ross multiple millions to promote the site

tweets.author: @benhorney
tweets.text: Fascinating look at one (shady) way Polymarket has tried to market itself. Also fascinating: WSJ's publisher is Dow Jones, which in January announced a prediction-market partnership with Polymarket. That deal didn't stop WSJ from this investigative report (a win for journalism)

tweets.author: @mikeisaac
tweets.text: seeing limp attempts to defend polymarket here with a “all companies use deceptive advertising” feint not exactly! there are FTC, FCC and FDA guidelines around certain types of commercials, not to mention civil suits i imagine this graf will eventually be read in a courtroom [image]

top news.title: Sources: John Ternus gets ready to put his firm imprint on Apple's industrial design team, which has lost a true seat at Apple's exec table over the past decade

tweets.author: @markgurman
tweets.text: The craziest part about the Siri delay is they said they postponed it for two years because it only worked 2/3 of the time. The other Apple Intelligence features were even worse than that before the new iOS.

tweets.author: @markgurman
tweets.text: Apple has big plans in store for the rest of 2026, 2027 and 2028, including several new iPhones, Macs, iPads, AI wearables, home devices and more. Here's a list of some of what to expect in the latest Power On -

tweets.author: @_thejasonc
tweets.text: For those who question my perspective on John Ternus... Mark Gurman just wrote an article arguing that Apple may need Ternus to shake up its product roadmap and design culture.  I've said it before: Apple doesn't need another Tim Cook.  Apple needs someone who can identify what comes NEXT [image]

top news.title: A speculative scenario titled “Europe 2031” projects economic and political instability in the EU if it fails to keep pace with the US and China in the AI race

tweets.author: @deanwball
tweets.text: Extremely cogent and well-written scenario, starting from the present, warning about Europe's dangerous trajectory. I was in Paris for the AI Summit after DeepSeek r1, and I can attest that the level of delusion about what that model meant was exactly as this scenario describes.

tweets.author: @dadajudith
tweets.text: In the morning, European citizens will wake up and find their access to Claude Mythos/ Fable gone. Nobody asked us. Nobody had to. We wrote Europe 2031 precisely for this moment.

tweets.author: @leemakiyama
tweets.text: This is a very interesting story about Europe failing to catch up on AI compute capacity / capability, pointed to me by @marconav. The only caveat I have is how it makes the same mistake as EU policy: obsessing over European supply and largely ignoring the demand side.
